cases.statement: One affected heterozygous male (P42, family F26) in the Japanese national survey.

people.label: P42 (family F26)
people.zygosity_or_genotype: heterozygous (cohort-level statement that all 54 patients were heterozygous)
people.key_phenotypes: onset 14 yr; paroxysmal recurrent fever; oral and genital ulcers; arthralgia; initial diagnosis tonsillitis

quotes.quote: | F26 | P42 | M | 14 yr | p.M174fs | TAC | Colchicine, MTX |  |

phenotype_specificity.statement: Cohort-level only: the survey enrolled patients whose HA20 diagnosis was confirmed by functional analysis; TNFAIP3 was Sanger-sequenced or tested on an autoinflammatory gene panel. Results for other genes in this person are not reported.

quotes.quote: The diagnosis of HA20 was confirmed via functional analysis of the TNFAIP3 variant.
Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood for sequencing of all exons and exon-intron junctions of *TNFAIP3*.

Regarding recently identified cases, next-generation sequencing of target genes related to autoinflammatory disorders, including *TNFAIP3*, was performed at the Kazusa DNA Laboratory (Kisarazu, Japan).

segregation.statement: Not stated in the text (P42 is the only listed member of F26). Cohort-level penetrance figure only.

quotes.quote: Additionally, family analysis revealed that three cases with heterozygous variants were asymptomatic (penetrance: 95.7%).

functional.statement: No result for this specific variant is stated in the text. The paper says newly identified variants were tested with an NF-κB reporter assay in A20-deficient HEK293 cells (constructs) and that patients whose variant could not be confirmed were excluded; the per-variant results are only in Figure 2, whose labels are not in the text available. Cohort-level method statements only.

quotes.quote: To confirm the pathogenicity of newly identified *TNFAIP3* variants, excluding cases of large deletions and known variants, nuclear factor (NF)-κB-driven luciferase reporter gene assays employing A20-deficient HEK293 cells were performed, as previously described (2).
Patients carrying *TNFAIP3* variants with pathogenicity that could not be confirmed by this functional analysis were excluded from this study.
The results of functional analyses of newly identified TNFAIP3 variants are shown in Figure 2 and Supplementary Figure 2.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Single-nucleotide deletion causing a frameshift, predicted p.(Met174TrpfsTer42) (batch HGVS). Disease mechanism as stated in the papers: heterozygous loss of function (haploinsufficiency).

quotes.quote: A20 haploinsufficiency (HA20) is a hereditary autoinflammatory disease caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in the TNFAIP3 gene (1).

authors_classification.statement: Cohort-level only: the authors describe all 35 distinct variants in the 54 surveyed patients with the words quoted. No per-variant ACMG criteria are stated.

quotes.quote: All 54 patients analyzed had heterozygous variants in TNFAIP3, comprising a total of 35 distinct pathogenic variants.

concerns: Appears only in the survey's supplementary table and pedigree figure; no case narrative and no prior report cited for family F26.
Whether c.520delA was among the variants tested in Figure 2 is not stated in the text.
No transcript is named in the paper.
notes_for_panel: Single affected carrier with Behçet-like features; no variant-specific functional or family data in the text.
